svg.text: EchoVault — Browser→Server End-to-End Channel · Layered Architecture (v3)
BIP-39 identity → authenticated HPKE seal (RFC 9180 · ChaCha20-Poly1305) inside TLS 1.3 · hpke-js ⇄ pyhpke · defeats a TLS-terminating proxy
THE STACK (in the browser · top → bottom)
Renders prompt/echo; E2E ON/OFF toggle for the demo.
Framing, monotonic seq, replay-reject, tamper-fail, ratchet.
Seal/Open via hpke-js ⇄ pyhpke; AAD binds context.
Pin server key; sign+verify the transcript (Ed25519).
Outer wss tunnel; protects transport+metadata; ends at proxy.
frames carry { enc, ct } — sealed payload
Trust boundary = the process holding the recipient X25519 private key.
TLS alone moves that boundary to the proxy; the inner HPKE seal moves it back to the real reader — network, proxy, OS, and logs see ciphertext only (Layers L1 + L4 = the demo’s whole thesis).

v3: the handshake is Ed25519-authenticated against a pinned key, so a swapped /pubkey key is rejected (T11/P8). Honest remaining gap: served-JS / code-delivery — the server serves the JS that pins + seals; a static BIP-39 key alone has no forward secrecy (→ epoch-ratchet stretch).
